references.text: Daniel prophesies about the resurrection of the dead: "Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt." This is a central Old Testament text concerning the resurrection of the righteous, which Jesus refers to in [ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14] with the expression "the resurrection of the righteous" (ἀνάστασις τῶν δικαίων).

In [ref:Luk 6:35|Luke 6:35], Jesus says: "Do good and lend, expecting nothing in return." The same principle as in [ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14] – to act kindly without expecting repayment from people, because the reward comes from God.

[ref:Luk 6:38|Luke 6:38] promises that "it will be given to you" – God's recompense for generosity. This parallels the promise in [ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14] that it "will be repaid to you" (ἀνταποδοθήσεται σοι).

Jesus speaks in [ref:Joh 5:28-29|John 5:28-29] about all who are in the graves hearing his voice and coming out – those who have done good, to the resurrection of life. This expands on the idea of the resurrection of the righteous mentioned in [ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14].

Paul confesses before Felix in [ref:Apg 24:15|Acts 24:15] that he has hope in God that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous. The expression "the resurrection of the righteous" is directly linked to Jesus' words in [ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14].

[ref:Hebr 11:35|Hebrews 11:35] mentions that women received their dead back by resurrection, and that some were tortured "to obtain a better resurrection". The hope of a future reward at the resurrection is the same motive found in [ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14].

[ref:Åp 20:6|Revelation 20:6] speaks of the first resurrection and calls those who share in it "blessed" (μακάριος) – the same word used in [ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14], where Jesus says "you will be blessed" (μακάριος ἔσῃ), referring to the resurrection of the righteous.

[ref:Ordsp 19:17|Proverbs 19:17] says: "Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord, and he will reward them for what they have done." This supports the principle in [ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14] that God himself rewards those who give to those who cannot repay.

The beatitudes in [ref:Matt 5:3-12|Matthew 5:3-12] repeatedly use the word μακάριος and promise heavenly reward to those who suffer and show mercy. The same structure – a blessing with an eschatological reward – is found in [ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14].

[ref:Jes 3:10|Isaiah 3:10] assures that it will go well for the righteous, for they shall enjoy the fruit of their deeds. God's just reward to the righteous is the same theme as the promise in [ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14].
